transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-29
Time: 14:30 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Marsh (Redwood SE), Devon Cho (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Orion Head of ML), Markus Li (Orion Platform Eng), Priya Reddy (Orion CTO), Ethan Park (Orion Security)

Summary: Quick sign-off on POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Agreed go/no-go thresholds, data and bench harness handoffs, and reporting format. Action items assigned and schedule for first benchmark run.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, reporting format, timelines, security/egress, dedicated test capacity

Action items (recap): see metadata list above

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, goal is to get final sign-off on the POC success criteria and acceptance tests so we can kick off benching early Jan.
[00:12] Lina: Sounds good. We've reviewed the draft you sent, we have a couple clarifying q's around the thresholds and also the reporting format.
[00:20] Samir: Great, Jenna will run through the acceptance tests and the exact metrics; I'll handle commercial and timeline bits. Jenna?
[00:27] Jenna: Yep, thanks. So high level our POC acceptance is split into functional correctness, latency/throughput (performance), and stability/observability. We'll use the benchmark harness to run a set of workloads representative of your production traffic.
[00:39] Markus: Quick check — this is going to run against Redwood Dedicated test nodes, correct? We don't want noisy shared hosts.
[00:46] Jenna: Correct, dedicated test pool. We'll provision a temporary Dedicated slice with the same instance types we propose for prod. We'll also capture KV cache warmups and steady-state runs.
[00:58] Ethan: From security, we need to ensure that the test bucket is in our account and that logs and artifacts go to our S3 and not Redwood's. Also SAML single sign-on needs to be available for the console.
[01:09] Devon: Yep, we can do customer-managed S3 and we support SSO/SAML. We'll also provide an export of raw bench results so you can ingest into your tools.
[01:18] Priya: Back to criteria, what's the p95 latency threshold and the tolerance? We saw in the doc p95 < 200ms but want to confirm at what seq len and model.
[01:27] Jenna: Good call. For this POC we're using the 2-step acceptance: model variant A (open-llm-13B-like) and variant B (quantized 8-bit) — we'll measure on a 256-token context with typical prompt lengths. p95 generation latency must be < 220ms for interactive evals, and tail behavior p99 < 450ms. Go/no-go requires both: p95 below threshold AND less than 2% error rates for hallucination tests.
[01:48] Lina: 220ms seems aggressive for our current infra — are you including network? What about cold-starts?
[01:55] Jenna: Measurements are server-side only (no client network). We'll run cold-start (cold containers after idle) and steady-state runs; acceptance is based on steady-state for SLA comparison. Cold-starts should be documented but not blocker unless they exceed 10x normal latency.
[02:08] Markus: Throughput targets? We need to ensure it can sustain our spike load of about 60 requests per second at 95% of traffic patterns.
[02:16] Jenna: For the POC we'll define a throughput bench: steady-state sustained throughput of 1800 requests per minute (30 rps) with p95 < 220ms. For burst tests we'll run 60 rps for 5 minutes to validate autoscaling behavior and no more than 5% error rate. Those numbers map to your stated expected traffic and safety margin.
[02:37] Priya: And quality metrics — how are we measuring hallucinations or incorrect outputs?
[02:42] Jenna: We'll use a labeled test set of 1200 prompts with human-evaluated ground truth and automated rubrics. Acceptance requires macro-accuracy > 92% on extraction tasks and a hallucination rate < 2%. We'll deliver the scorer and the CSV of judgments.
[02:56] Lina: Ok, reporting format — we want percentile breakdowns and raw samples. What's in the report?
[03:01] Samir: Final report will be a zipped artifact: CSV of raw request logs (timestamps, latencies, model variant), aggregated percentiles (p50/p75/p90/p95/p99) per workload, error rates, and a quality sheet with sample outputs and human labels. Also a short slide deck with conclusions and recommended sizing for prod.
[03:18] Markus: Please include memory/CPU/GPU utilization traces and exact machine types used — our infra team needs that to size clusters.
[03:24] Jenna: Yep, we'll include sysmetrics with 10s granularity and an inference profile including KV cache hit rates, batch sizes, and GPU memory footprints.
[03:34] Ethan: On encryption and logs: ensure logs are stored encrypted at rest, and we need an audit log of access to the bench results.
[03:40] Devon: Logs exported to your S3 will be SSE-KMS encrypted and we can add a separate audit log feed we push to your syslog or cloudwatch as requested.
[03:50] Lina: Timelines — once we sign-off today, how soon can you get the harness running?
[03:54] Samir: We're targeting first bench run the week of 2026-01-06. Jenna's team can provision the dedicated test slice in 3 business days after we receive the sample data and the S3 creds.
[04:05] Jenna: I'll also need a mapping document of prompt types and the priority buckets. That should arrive with the dataset.
[04:11] Priya: For acceptance sign-off — who's on the panel and what is the decision gate?
[04:15] Lina: We expect sign-off from Priya (CTO), Lina (Head of ML) and one platform representative (Markus). If the run meets the thresholds, it's a go; if not, we'll triage and decide whether to tune config or move to a pilot with guarded traffic.
[04:30] Samir: To clarify the go/no-go logic: go if all required checks pass (performance thresholds + quality thresholds + no critical security issues). If one of the metrics misses by less than 5% we allow a single remediation run with config tweaks; missing by more than 5% triggers a remediation plan and a joint review.
[04:48] Jenna: We'll also provide the raw benchmark harness so you can re-run in your environment; the harness publishes a standard CSV and also a JSON summary. For the acceptance artifact we'll include: results.csv, summary.json, sysmetrics.csv, and a slides.pdf.
[05:03] Lina: One more on metrics: how will you measure latency percentiles — is aggregation per-request or per-user-session?
[05:09] Jenna: Per-request. We'll tag requests by workload type and compute percentiles per-workload. We'll also provide session-aggregates if you prefer to see end-to-end user latency.
[05:19] Markus: Any limitations on model variants? For example, quantized runs might change quality. Are both variants required for acceptance?
[05:25] Jenna: We proposed two variants for the POC — baseline float model and an optimized quantized model. Acceptance requires the baseline to meet quality thresholds; quantized model must meet either equivalent quality or within a 1-2% quality delta while improving cost/latency. If quantized drops quality more than 2%, it's a fail for that variant but doesn't necessarily fail the whole POC if baseline passes and we agree on next steps.
[05:46] Priya: Security checklist — SOC2 relevant controls, key management, SSO, network egress controls. We need your security pack.
[05:52] Samir: We'll send the security pack after the call; we'll include SOC2 attestation, KMS flow, and network diagrams.
[05:58] Ethan: Also need assurance logs for admin access during bench.
[06:02] Devon: We'll provide an access log and can run the bench under a read-only service account you own.
[06:07] Lina: Ok, final sign-off language — we need a single doc with the checkboxes so our legal/product folks can sign. Can you produce that?
[06:13] Samir: Yes, I'll send a sign-off template. We'll add exact numeric thresholds and acceptance gates.
[06:18] Priya: Any remarks on cost incurred for this bench run? If dedicated nodes are provisioned, will there be charges?
[06:23] Samir: For the POC Redwood can provide test credit to cover the initial dedicated capacity for the first two benchmark runs. Any additional runs or extended dedicated time would be billed per our dedicated pricing. We'll include a cost estimate in the follow-up.
[06:36] Markus: Good. Can we get a short sample of the report format — just one workload example — so we know how it looks?
[06:41] Jenna: I can share a sample results.csv and the slides. I'll anonymize client data.
[06:45] Lina: Also, in the success criteria doc you mentioned a pass threshold for stability — what is that again?
[06:50] Jenna: Stability acceptance: no more than 1 unexplained outage or fatal error during the bench, and error rate < 1% for steady-state. If we see config-related errors we'll classify and allow a single remediation attempt.
[07:03] Priya: That's fair. Anything else on the scope?
[07:07] Samir: Quick recap of what we'll send: final success criteria doc, sign-off template, security pack, benchmark harness and sample dataset checklist. First bench run targeted week of 2026-01-06. Action items assigned.
[07:18] Lina: We agree, pending receipt of data and security docs.
[07:22] Priya: OK, sign-off conditional, sounds good.
[07:25] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts today and set up the bench window.
[07:29] Jenna: Thanks all.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker mislabels and a few product names like "KV cash" or "Kuberntes" may appear; the team confirmed intended terms where relevant in the call.
